findings.message: The production drain and serve pipeline build their routed CliClient and Registry in `squatch.stages.compose` (`registry = Registry(config)`; `CliClient(registry, ...)`; `WatchdogLLM` wrapping). `squatch/merge.py:457` `compose_pipeline` reaches it. Cooldown-aware candidate selection and quota-cooldown arming on the real implement/review calls must be wired here. The criterion that drain and serve use the same provider registry payload at their composition roots also forces this file. Neither `squatch/stages.py` nor `squatch/merge.py` is in the fence.
findings.paved_road: Add `squatch/stages.py` and `squatch/merge.py` to the Scope fence as the production client composition owners. Because embedding them would breach headroom, list them as measured on-demand inspection exceptions with their authoring-time sizes.

findings.message: The live Timers instance exists only as a local variable inside `restart_session` (`deadlines = timers(recovered.journal)`), which `squatch/daemon.py:363` `compose_daemon_restart` composes. It is not exposed on `Session` or to any composition root. A provider cooldown cannot arm a journaled Timer on the lock holder's single Timers instance without changing that seam. Arming a second Timers instance over the same journal would break the re-arm-exactly-once contract that `tests/test_restart_timers.py` pins. `squatch/restart.py` and `squatch/daemon.py` are unfenced.
findings.paved_road: Fence the module owning the Timers lifetime seam (`squatch/restart.py` and/or `squatch/daemon.py`, plus `squatch/runner.py` if `Session` carries it), and state how the session-owned Timers instance reaches the provider client. Alternatively, have Scope in state explicitly that cooldown is re-derived from the journal's `timer_armed` records through the existing fold, without a second live Timers owner.

findings.message: `Serve.compose` builds its own separate `Registry(config)` and two more `CliClient`s, for the rework Driver and Triage. Its pipeline's client comes from `stages.compose` through the pipeline factory. The ticket does not say which of these construction sites the single-registry criterion covers, or whether Triage/rework calls also fail over. Without that, the Definition-of-rejected line 'separate drain and serve registry payloads' is ambiguous.
findings.paved_road: Name every provider-client construction site in scope (`stages.compose`, `Serve.compose` rework/triage, `__main__._triage_pass`). State that the acceptance test asserts they share one registry/cooldown payload, or scope the non-pipeline sites out explicitly.
